Native relay troubleshooting

Diagnose native relay sessions, stream ends, lost requests, transport counters and logs.

About 9 min read · 6 sections

On this page

Return to the native connected-machine overview.

Session diagnostics

The relay records timestamped, fixed lifecycle causes in its existing private managed stderr log. Records cover session start/end, queue saturation, auth scope changes, frame failures, child exit, and task panic. Real queued SDK lifecycle events may include canonical thread and turn IDs. Queue acceptance does not prove that the frontend received or rendered an event.

Child stderr is drained with bounded buffers. Only aggregate byte/chunk counts and whether draining finished are recorded; raw errors, prompt text, tool arguments, credentials, environment values, paths, and labels are excluded. Thirty-second activity records distinguish quiet active work from an ended session. Reconnect cleanup checks task identity before cancelling a connection; an older task cannot cancel its replacement. Separate limits bound active and retiring sessions. Fair event selection keeps Stop and steering requests from being starved by continuous child output.

The adapter reports a genuine unfinished native executor exit as an error and failed turn before shutting its client down. Buffered SDK completion events are drained first, and intentional shutdown does not manufacture a failure. The error says the Codex engine stopped (the app may have restarted it), that the chat's history is saved, and that sending a message continues it; a chat on a connected machine reconnects that computer if it stays unavailable. The same text serves local chats, whose engine the app restarts by itself, for example on "Authenticated workspace changed". A relay disconnect alone does not establish whether shared work stopped, so the relay does not manufacture a completed or failed task from that observation.

Stream ends

Each remote client stream maps to one relay session. When the relay side ends a stream, the patched SDK tells the client right away: it forwards the replies already queued for that stream, then sends Pong { status: unknown } for it. The client closes the stream with "became unknown", fails its own pending requests, and reconnects after about one second. Before this change the SDK forgot the stream silently, and the client lost every request it sent until its next 30-second ping.

Stream ended by Unknown pong
Shim child exit, session rejection, queue failure, relay shutdown, inbound-gap reset, relay idle release Yes, after the queued replies
Client close, idle sweep (10 minutes), re-initialize of the same stream, SDK shutdown No

The SDK's idle sweep only sees streams while its cloud websocket is connected. While that connection fails, for example with 409 Conflict, an unused stream used to stay open and keep its codex-shim and engine release alive for hours, which held rollouts at process_version_pending. The relay now releases a session itself (session_ended with cause idle_released) after 10 minutes in which no frame moved in either direction, no turn is running, and no request or approval waits for an answer. A turn that started without a matching completion keeps the session. The phone reconnects on its next use and gets an engine from the current release.

The tracker marks a stream before it ends it itself, so only relay-side ends send the pong. Every step is bounded by one 750 ms budget: forwarding the queued replies, queueing the pong, and waiting for the websocket writer to confirm it. Replies or a pong that miss the budget are dropped and counted, so a full queue or a stalled writer cannot keep a stream open. A re-initialized stream with the same client and stream ID is no longer closed when its predecessor's task finishes, and the old stream's chunk state is cleared when the new initialize arrives, so a restarted sequence cannot be mistaken for duplicates.

On shutdown the relay first ends every session, which sends the unknown pongs, then reads transport events for up to one second until each stream reports ConnectionClosed. The SDK emits that event only after the pong was written or its budget ran out. Streams that open during that second are refused the same way, and their requests are counted. Only then does the relay stop the SDK.

The pong only shortens detection. A relay restart still ends every stream, and an initialize sent while no relay is running waits for the next relay. Children that keep failing at startup now cause client reconnects paced by the client's backoff (one to twenty seconds) instead of its 30-second ping; compare streamEndNotified with session_rejected records when that happens.

Transport counters

session_activity (every 30 seconds per session) and session_ended records carry a transport object. A transport_activity record with the same object is written every 30 seconds whenever it changed, including when no session is open. Values are totals since the relay started.

Key Counts
inboundSeqDedupeDrops Client messages the SDK dropped because their sequence number was at or below the last delivered one
inboundLateFillDeduped Of those, messages that filled a known hole: they arrived late and out of order
inboundChunkDedupeDrops Chunks of an already completed chunked message
unknownStreamDrops Client messages for a stream the SDK did not know (only initialize opens one)
unknownStreamPings Pings for an unknown stream, answered with an unknown pong
streamEndNotified Relay-side stream ends that ran the unknown-pong path
streamEndPongQueued, streamEndPongWritten, streamEndPongUnconfirmed, streamEndPongDropped What happened to those pongs within the budget
streamEndDrained, streamEndDrainDropped Queued replies forwarded or dropped before the pong
pingsWithSeq, pingsWithoutSeq, messagesWithoutSeq Client envelopes on tracked streams with or without a sequence number
holesOpened, missingSeqs, holesFilled Sequence gaps seen, the sequence numbers they span, and gaps filled later
holesStale, holesFilledAfterStale, holesUnresolvedAtClose, holeOverflows Gaps older than 15 seconds, gaps filled after that, gaps still open when the stream closed, and gaps not tracked past 64 per stream
inboundGapResets, inboundGapResetsSuppressed Streams ended by reset mode, and resets skipped by the ten-minute limit
outboundUnacked, outboundUnackedMax Envelopes waiting for a backend acknowledgement now and at most; the SDK writer stops at 128
noSessionDrops Client messages for a connection with no relay session
shutdownRefusedStreams Streams refused while the relay was shutting down
inboundGapResetMode Whether the reset switch file exists

Lost-request detection

Some client requests never reach the host. The detector shows where they go missing without changing what the SDK delivers. For each stream with an explicit stream ID, it records every client sequence number the host sees: messages, completed chunked messages, pings, and client closes. Acknowledgements carry server sequence numbers and are ignored. A gap below the highest number seen is a hole; it exists only because a later envelope arrived.

A hole is stale when it stays unfilled for 15 seconds and no chunk of that stream arrived in the last 15 seconds. The check runs on every envelope and on the SDK's 30-second sweep. Each stale hole is logged once. A loss is detected only after a later envelope arrives, so the worst case is about 15 seconds plus a 30-second ping plus the 30-second sweep. A message the client never numbered, or that never reached the host, cannot be seen.

The detector rests on one unverified assumption: that the backend forwards ping sequence numbers. The first ping on each stream logs ping_seq_presence. If pingsWithoutSeq grows, or pings with sequence numbers leave holes on healthy streams, the detector would misreport, and reset mode must stay off.

Reset switch

Reset mode is off by default. While the file inbound-gap-reset exists in the relay home, a stale hole ends its stream through the unknown-pong path, so the client fails the stuck requests and reconnects. The file is checked when a hole turns stale, so no restart is needed:

touch RELAY_HOME/inbound-gap-reset   # enable
trash RELAY_HOME/inbound-gap-reset   # disable

The relay home is the relayHome that gateway native install reports; it also holds status.json. Only a regular file enables the switch. Each stream is reset at most once in ten minutes. A reset fails every pending request on that stream, including a turn/start whose turn may already be running in the shared executor, so a user retry can duplicate that turn. No JSON-RPC result or turn event is ever invented.

Enable it only after log-only data shows pingsWithoutSeq at 0 and almost no stale holes on healthy streams, including across host reconnects.

Reading the logs

The relay writes one JSON record per line, prefixed with gateway: , to its managed log. Each record is written with a single write, so records no longer splice, and a daemon no longer prints remote-client-connected to the same file.

Records with "scope":"native_relay" are the relay's own: session lifecycle, session_activity, session_ended, and transport_activity. Records with "scope":"native_relay_sdk" and "event":"sdk_log" come from the SDK transport. They carry a fixed label, the level, and only allowlisted fields. SDK message text is never printed; a warning without a known label appears as unlisted with its source file and line. Each label prints at most 20 lines a minute, and the next line reports the rest as suppressed.

Label Meaning
rc_connecting, rc_connected, rc_cycle_ended, rc_status_changed Host websocket lifecycle; connectionEndReason and reconnectAttempt explain reconnects
rc_connect_failed A connect attempt failed. The SDK's error text is never printed: errorClass names its kind (ws_auth, ws_http, ws_tls, ws_io, ws_dns, ws_protocol, refresh_http, refresh_transport, refresh_parse, refresh_mismatch, auth_recovery or unclassified) and httpStatus the 3-digit status for ws_auth, ws_http and refresh_http. ws_http with httpStatus 409 means another engine holds this Mac's remote-control connection
rc_writer_disconnected, rc_reader_disconnected The host websocket dropped; errorKind is TimedOut (no websocket pong for 60 seconds), UnexpectedEof (stream ended), ConnectionAborted (close frame), or InvalidData (read error)
stream_end_notified A relay-side stream end: reason, replies drained and drainDropped, and the pong outcome
inbound_hole_stale A stale hole: first missing number, size, age, highest number seen, ping counts, reset mode, and the action taken
inbound_hole_filled_late A stale hole was filled later, after waitedMs
inbound_late_fill_deduped, inbound_seq_dedupe_drop The SDK dropped a message at or below its delivered mark; the first means it filled a hole
unknown_stream_drop, inbound_gap_reset, ping_seq_presence Unknown-stream drops, resets (or suppressed resets), and whether a stream's pings carry numbers

Late fills and deduped late fills mean the backend reordered envelopes; stale holes that are never filled mean the envelopes were lost before the host. An outboundUnacked near 128 means the backend stopped acknowledging and the SDK writer is gated for every stream. The backend may never acknowledge a pong sent to a stream the client already closed; if outboundUnackedMax keeps rising after unknown pongs, that is the cause.

Client and stream IDs appear only as 12-character hashes with a per-process salt. The same ID has the same hash in every record of one relay process (client and stream in gateway labels, clientId and streamId in SDK labels), and a new hash after a restart. Counters, labels, numbers, durations, and fixed reasons are the only other content: no tokens, bodies, arguments, URLs, paths, or account, server, or environment identifiers.
